To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the low-frequency (0.04-0.15 Hz) band in the power spectrum of HRV is a poor indicator of autonomic outflow and should be avoided, (2) equivalent normalized low-frequency (LFnu), normalized high-frequency (HFnu) or ratio variables (LF/HF or HF/LF) should be used with extreme caution, and (3) the experimental design and analysis of short-term HRV studies should be improved.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) the use of the term “low-frequency” power (LF) and “high-frequency” power (HF) as a measure of autonomic outflow and the interpretation of the LF/HF ratio; (ii) the use of equivalent normalized LF (LFnu) and HF (HFnu) terms; and (iii) the lack of experimental control over extraneous factors that influence HRV.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of frequency-domain HRV in the short term is a poor method for the assessment of autonomic outflow and that the use of LF/HF ratio is not justified.
the field has not made sufficient progress to warrant the continued use of the ratio and LFnu/HFnu variables in HRV research.
the use of HRV in the short-term frequency domain should be considered with extreme caution.
